months.2: February remains cool, making the exposed coastal paths around Cap Ferrat pleasant for a brisk walk.
months.11: November cools into the 60s, offering comfortable walking along the coastal peninsulas.

north-cascades.overview: The North Cascades offer dramatic alpine hiking, with steep trails leading to jagged peaks, deep valleys, and hanging glaciers. Day hikes like the long, steep climb up Sahale Arm or the shorter Cascade Pass deliver views of a vast, icy wilderness. The season is short, dictated by heavy winter snows that close the main highway for months, making late summer the only reliable window for the high country.

months.1: The main highway through the park is closed for the winter. Hiking is limited to snowshoe routes on the periphery, such as near the Mount Baker ski area, while the interior is inaccessible.
months.2: Deep snow keeps the North Cascades Highway closed and the interior inaccessible. Only snowshoe routes on the outer edges, near the Mount Baker ski area, are practical.
months.3: The highway stays closed under winter snowpack, and the interior remains out of reach. Snowshoeing near the Mount Baker ski area is the main option.
months.8: This is the prime month for hiking the North Cascades. The high alpine trails, including the steep trek up Sahale Arm, are entirely clear of snow, giving access to the dramatic glacier-carved landscape.

north-island.overview: The North Island is anchored by the Tongariro Alpine Crossing, a long day hike past volcanic craters and emerald lakes, usually walked point to point with a shuttle at the trailhead. Trekkers can extend this into the multi-day Tongariro Northern Circuit, or head west to Mount Taranaki for the demanding two-to-three-day Pouakai Circuit. The best conditions run from December to March, while the high volcanic routes become hazardous and require technical gear from June to September.

months.2: Warm, dry days continue to provide excellent conditions on the high volcanic routes. The multi-day Tongariro Northern Circuit is fully open.
months.11: Warmer days melt the remaining snow on the main volcanic routes, opening up the Tongariro Alpine Crossing for standard hiking. The emerald lakes become fully visible again.
months.12: Long daylight hours and warming temperatures bring prime conditions back to the high trails. The multi-day circuits and long volcanic day hikes are fully accessible, offering expansive views across the island.

nova-scotia.overview: Nova Scotia's best walking traces the rugged Atlantic coastline and the highlands of Cape Breton. The famous Skyline Trail offers a short, dramatic loop above the Gulf of St. Lawrence, where walkers often spot moose and whales from the headland boardwalks. Other day hikes along the Cabot Trail lead through deep river canyons and coastal forests.

months.7: The hiking season hits its peak with warm, clear days perfect for the Cabot Trail routes. Skyline Trail parking needs a timed reservation through the summer.
months.8: Warm weather continues, making this an ideal time for coastal walks and highland loops. Skyline Trail parking still needs a timed reservation.
months.9: Crisp air and clear skies provide excellent walking conditions. The coastal views are sharp, and the highland trails remain fully accessible, with Skyline Trail parking by reservation.
months.11: Freezing temperatures return and the autumn leaves drop. Trails are often icy, marking the end of the main walking season in the highlands.

nyc.overview: Walking here means easy nature paths within the five boroughs: the wooded trails of Inwood Hill Park, the Staten Island Greenbelt and the paved loops of Central Park. All are reached by subway or ferry and offer a break from the pavement, though they stay firmly urban.

months.2: The cold continues through February, keeping the park trails often frozen.
months.5: May offers pleasant walking weather, with lush greenery filling out the wooded paths of Inwood Hill Park.

months.4: Temperatures and humidity increase, making the steeper forest trails more tiring, but the coastal walks remain pleasant.
months.6: The rainy season continues, keeping the forest trails muddy and slippery. High heat and humidity make any long walk uncomfortable.
months.7: Intense heat and high humidity make hiking punishing and unpleasant. The risk of typhoons also begins to rise, threatening trail closures.
